For each component, agents first create an Isabelle/HOL theory with a specification, a soundness proof, and a reference checker made by code generation, then a fast Rust implementation, verified with Verus against a specification that mirrors the Isabelle definitions line by line. Specifications are frozen after independent review and cannot be changed by the implementing agents. A trust manifest lists what is still trusted. We built trust chains for SAT (verified LRAT checking); SMT, with certificates from an extended z3 and verified bit-blasting for bit-vectors and floating point; answer-set programming, with native certificates from clingo, including weight rules and optimality; and, closing the loop, Verus's final verification-condition step, by translation validation. All 3,726 SMT queries from 20 crates are certified and validated, and 15,662 answer-set proofs are accepted by both the Isabelle and the Verus checker. We found soundness defects in three proof checkers, including drat-trim, and in five solvers, including clasp and z3, which report wrong unsatisfiability.

papers.title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
papers.summary: In this note, we prove an Erdős-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.

papers.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
papers.summary: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

papers.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
papers.summary: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
papers.summary: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression.

papers.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
papers.summary: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

papers.title: Rate--burst safety languages: the Farey structure of the burst boundary and discrimination under erasures
papers.summary: A leaky-bucket constraint with rate \(ρ\) and burst \(B\) allows at most \(ρn+B\) costly steps in every window of \(n\) consecutive steps. The infinite 0/1 words that satisfy it form a safety language. For a finite graph with edge costs 0 and 1, we study the least burst at which the cost word of some infinite path lies in this language, as a function of the real rate. This function is the exact tolerance of a monitor that distinguishes two finite-state systems observed through an erasure channel with a leaky-bucket bound. The language is \(ω\)-regular at every rational rate but not at irrational rates once the burst reaches 1, so ultimately periodic witnesses do not come from automata theory. We prove directly that simple lassos suffice at all real rates and that all breakpoints of the boundary lie in the Farey sequence of order N for a graph with N vertices. One lasso has a tight bound of order N to the power 2/3 on its affine pieces, whereas the choice among paths creates downward jumps and boundaries that are neither convex nor concave. One evaluation at the mediant of each Farey interval recovers the affine piece and an optimal lasso, and a greatest-fixed-point computation over decreasing integer bursts yields the whole function in polynomial time and linear working space. We also compute discrimination horizons and extend the Farey structure to turn-based safety games.

papers.title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
papers.summary:
For a real number $α>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $ρ(G)=α$ and maximum degree $Δ(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=α-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=αI-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. Assume that $αI-A(T)\succ0$ for every attached tree $T$. For each $z\in V(H)$, let $q_{z,1},\ldots,q_{z,s_z}$ be the positive root pivots obtained by the scalar tree recursion for the trees attached to $z$, and set
  \[
  a_z=α-\sum_{j=1}^{s_z}q_{z,j}^{-1},
  \qquad
  M_H(\mathbf a)=\operatorname{diag}(a_z:z\in V(H))-A(H),
  \] where an empty sum is zero. Then $ρ(G)=α$ if and only if $M_H(\mathbf a)\succeq0$ and $\det M_H(\mathbf a)=0$. Taking $H=K_1$ recovers the tree criteria, while $δ(H)\geq2$ gives criteria for graphs with prescribed 2-core $H$. In particular, for unicyclic graphs of prescribed cycle length, path continuants reduce the spectral condition to positivity inequalities and one scalar equation.

papers.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
papers.summary: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

papers.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
papers.summary: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.

papers.title: The Schürmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
papers.summary: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Schürmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

papers.title: A $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for Weighted 3-Set Packing
papers.summary: We give a deterministic $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted $3$-set packing, for every fixed rational $\varepsilon>0$, improving on the 1.6908-approximation reported by Tong and Xu (2026). The algorithm has two phases. It first performs bounded local search using a rounded $12/7$-power potential. It then combines compatible exchanges that insert at most three sets and increase the original weight. The analysis relates the gap left by the first phase to the gain available to the second phase. We prove a structural inequality that bounds the weight of a comparison packing by $3/2$ times the current weight plus one sixth of a sum of small-exchange gains. Each gain accounts for all sets that the exchange must delete. A greedy rule recovers enough of these gains to obtain the approximation guarantee. We derive the structural bound from local optimality by analyzing finite computation trees and averaging the error caused by their limited depth. The running time is $n^{4^{O(1/\varepsilon)}}\operatorname{poly}(L)$, where $n$ is the number of input sets and $L$ is the input encoding length. The same guarantee holds for maximum-weight independent set in induced $K_{1,4}$-free graphs.

papers.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
papers.summary:
Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[
  |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

papers.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
papers.summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
papers.summary: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.

papers.title: Bound to be Complete: Efficient Verification for SQL Equivalence via U-Expressions
papers.summary:
Automated verification of SQL query equivalence is a fundamental problem in database area. Recent works developed verifiers with guaranteed completeness, which can generate counterexamples to disprove non-equivalent queries and are useful in various scenarios. However, they have to solve complex formulas and can fail to produce counterexamples within a reasonable time budget.
  This paper presents a new complete verifier called SQLution, which not only greatly reduces the verification time, but also supports more SQL features. The key insight is to represent SQL semantics using U-expression, a functional algebra that can model SQL with significantly simpler formulas than prior works, thereby leading to more efficient SMT solving. To turn this insight into a practical verifier, SQLution further tackles two technical challenges associated with modeling SQL using U-expression, namely, the lack of tuple ordering and the presence of unbounded summations. In particular, to support tuple ordering, SQLution proposes order semantics encoding which combines U-expressions with first-order logic. To handle unbounded summation, SQLution introduces unbounded summation expansion to transform them into bounded summations, which can be directly encoded into FOL formulas. Evaluation shows that compared with state-of-the-art verifiers, SQLution can support all 271 non-equivalent query pairs derived from the Spider dataset and reduces verification time by up to 98.6%.

papers.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
papers.summary:
For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--Rödl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $σ_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence.
  In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

papers.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
papers.summary: Let $Γ<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/Γ$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $Γ$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to Möbius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.

papers.title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
papers.summary:
We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[
  K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[
  χ(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to $5/4$.

papers.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
papers.summary: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

papers.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
papers.summary: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.title: Z[tau]-フォーム：Goodman-Strauss の Dodecafoam の正二十面体加群における算術としての定式化
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.summary: Goodman-Strauss の Dodecafoam は、正十二面体を大きさ tau^{-k}（tau=(1+√5)/2）の十二面体の泡で埋める置換規則であり、星形化の12平面が切り分ける7種類のセルを用いる。本論文ではこれを階数3の Z[tau]-加群の厳密な算術として書き換える。この加群は6本の五回軸が張る M であり、正二十面体群が GL(3,Z[tau]) の120個の行列として作用する。膨張したセルの配置がセルの和集合になるための必要十分条件は、そのファセット水準が {±1, ±tau³} に属し、かつ十二面体内に収まることである。この有限線形系を全スケールについて同時に解くことで、幾何学的探索で知られていた22個の規則が正確に得られ、スケール 1, tau, tau², tau³ 以外には規則が存在しないことが示される。置換は6つ組上の整数演算となり、幾何学的フォームの泡を正確に再現する。M の点が大きさ tau^{-k} の泡の中心かどうかは、フォームを構築せずに高々 k+3 個の厳密な符号ベクトル（アドレス）で判定でき、同一サイズの全泡は、ガロア共役が |x*| ≤ 2 tau^k を満たす M の点をふるい分けることで得られる（この上界は計算機支援で証明される）。大きさ tau^{-k} の泡の個数は A beta^k + O(|beta'|^k)（beta=(1+√29)/2）で漸近し、泡中心の再スケールされた共役の閉包はボックス次元が高々 log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3 であるため、泡は内部を持ついかなる cut-and-project 窓でも選別されない。1999年の論文の他のフォームは本フォームの部分フォームである。規則リストが許す50400個の置換は18899個の泡集合を与え、Dodecafoam は試験した深さまででそのうち13440個の積集合である。4次元では、120-cell の星形カットに対する同じ線形系が幾何学的探索の718個のクラスタを再現し、スケール sqrt(5) tau² を追加する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.appendix: 関連分野：aperiodic order and discrete patterns（置換タイリング、準結晶、cut-and-project）、combinatorics on words（置換規則・語の複雑性）、computer-assisted proofs（上界の計算機支援証明）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.title: {-1,0,1} を成分とする冪零三重対角行列
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.summary: 成分が {-1,0,1} である冪零三重対角行列をすべて決定する。対角成分 d と相対する非対角成分の積 b_k の組 (d,b) の集合 𝒩ₙ を、特性多項式が λⁿ となる条件で特徴づける。𝒩ₙ は n の偶奇に応じた2種類の明示的な「折り畳み」操作により 𝒩⌊n/2⌋ から得られることを示す。その結果、𝒩ₙ が空でないのは n=1 または 3·2ʲ-1 ≤ n ≤ 2ʲ⁺²-1（ある j≥0）のときに限られ、その場合の要素数は 2^⌊log₂n⌋ である。これにより {-1,0,1} 成分の冪零 n×n 三重対角行列の個数の公式が得られ、その値は 1,9,73,585,4809,39113 で始まる。d=0 の場合は先行論文で証明された Corless の予想である。主要な新要素は剛性現象で、n≥2 の組の特性多項式が mod 4 で λⁿ に合同ならば、それはより小さい組の折り畳みでなければならない。したがって特性多項式が mod 2^{1+⌊log₂n⌋} で λⁿ に合同ならば冪零となる。最後に、Corless の歪対称族に属する m×m 行列の固有値 0 の重複度は高々 2^{v₂(m+1)}-1 で、等号が達成されることを示す。分類、剛性命題、集合 𝒩ₙ の濃度、および mod 2^{1+⌊log₂n⌋} の判定法は Lean 4 で形式化されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.appendix: 関連分野: 列挙型組合せ論（冪零三重対角行列の計数）、計算機支援証明（Lean 4 による形式化）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.title: 3つのほぼ対称なメタタイルがSpectreタイリングを生成する
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.summary: Spectre非周期モノタイルに対する3つのメタタイルからなる系「D23」を提案する。これはhatタイリングに対するHTPF系と同様の概念であり、メタタイル自身が置換系を持ち、任意回数反復した後、最下位のメタタイルをSpectreタイルに変換できる。3つのメタタイルのうち1つは2回回転対称性を持ち、残り2つはそれぞれ2次と3次の「ほぼ対称」である。すなわち、タイルのn回デフレーションが覆う領域はその回転と完全には一致しないが、それらの共通部分内で不一致タイルの割合はn→∞で0に収束する。この近似的対称性はSpectreタイリング自体の近似的対称性に対応する。この系の興味深い性質として、3つのメタタイルのうち1つはSpectreへの変換で完全に消滅する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.appendix: 関連分野: aperiodic order and discrete patterns（非周期モノタイル・置換タイリング）。補足: 本論文は非周期モノタイルの置換構造と対称性の近似に関する研究であり、該当分野に直接関連する。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.title: エノン型自己同型写像に対する力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.summary: 複素アフィン平面上の多項式自己同型写像で力学次数が1より大きいものに対し、DujardinとFavreが提唱した力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想を証明した。すなわち、既約代数曲線がそのような自己同型写像の周期点を無限個含むのは、その曲線が、自己同型写像のある反復をその逆写像に共役させる多項式インボリューションの固定軌跡である場合に限ることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.appendix: 関連分野: arithmetic dynamics（力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想は周期点の分布に関する予想であり、本論文は複素力学系の枠組みでこれを扱っている）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.title: 非重複符号に関するBlackburn予想の証明
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.summary: 符号語の空でない真の接頭辞が他の符号語の接尾辞とならないような符号を非重複符号と呼ぶ。長さn、アルファベットサイズqの非重複符号の最大サイズSₙ(q)について、LevenshteinはSₙ(q) ≤ cₙqⁿ（ただしcₙ = (1/n)((n-1)/n)^(n-1)）を示した。アルファベットを分割するI, Jに対し符号I^(n-1)Jはnがqを割り切るときこの上界を達成し、Blackburnは任意のnと十分大きいqに対し最良のそのような符号が最大非重複符号であると予想した。本論文はこの予想を証明する。証明では極大非重複符号を記述する入れ子分割の生成関数を用いる。さらに、|I| = (n-1)q/nを満たす符号I^(n-1)Jとその反転のみがLevenshteinの上界を達成することを示す。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.appendix: 関連分野: combinatorics on words（符号理論・語の組合せ論）

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.title: レート・バースト安全言語：バースト境界のFarey構造と消失下での識別
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.summary: レートρとバーストBによるリーキーバケット制約は、任意の連続するnステップの窓において高コストのステップを高々ρn+B回まで許容する。この制約を満たす無限0/1語は安全言語を形成する。辺コストが0と1の有限グラフに対し、ある無限パスのコスト語がこの言語に属するような最小バーストを実レートの関数として研究する。この関数は、消失チャネルとリーキーバケット束縛を通して観測される2つの有限状態系を識別するモニタの正確な許容度を与える。言語はすべての有理レートでω正則であるが、バーストが1に達すると無理レートではω正則でなくなるため、最終周期的な証人はオートマトン理論からは得られない。すべての実レートで単純なlassoで十分であること、およびN頂点グラフに対して境界のすべてのブレークポイントが位数NのFarey列に属することを直接証明する。1つのlassoはそのアフィン片上でNの2/3乗オーダーのタイトな束縛を持つのに対し、パスの選択は下向きのジャンプと凸でも凹でもない境界を生み出す。各Farey区間の中間点での1回の評価でアフィン片と最適なlassoが回復され、減少する整数バースト上の最大不動点計算により多項式時間・線形作業空間で関数全体が得られる。さらに識別ホライズンを計算し、Farey構造を交代制安全ゲームへ拡張する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.appendix: 関連分野：combinatorics on words（語上の制約・言語）、symbolic dynamics（有限型シフトに関連する有限グラフ上の経路とω正則言語）、computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics（多項式時間アルゴリズムと不動点計算）、equational theories of words and monoids（安全言語の構造）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.conclusion: C2 上の Hénon 型多項式自己同型 f に対し、Dujardin–Favre の dynamical Manin–Mumford 予想を解決した論文。既約代数曲線 C が f の周期点を無限個含むのは、ある反転期をもつ多項式 involution σ の固定点になっている場合に限る（Theorem A）。数体上では Bogomolov 型の強化版（Theorem 5.5）も示す。算術力学・Hénon 写像・equidistribution に関心があるなら要読。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.main_claims: 主結果は Theorem A（p.2）: f が C2 の Hénon 型多項式自己同型、C が既約代数曲線のとき、C が f-周期点を無限個含む ⟺ ある r≥1 と多項式 involution σ が存在して Fix(σ)=C かつ σ∘f^r∘σ^{-1}=f^{-r}。逆向きは Dujardin–Favre [DF17, Prop 7.1] による。数体上では Theorem 5.5（p.15）: C(K) 上で h_f(p_n)→0 となる相異点列が存在する ⟺ 同様の σ が K 上定義され Fix(σ)=C、σ∘f^r∘σ^{-1}=f^{-r}。新規性は、DF が Jac(f) の代数性と Galois 共役の絶対値 1 までしか示せなかった状況で、完全な特徴づけを与えた点。鍵になる中間結果は Proposition 3.8（Green 関数の比例 G+ = αG−）、Proposition 4.1/4.2（Böttcher 座標の関係 (φ+∘f^N0)^A = (φ−∘f^{-N0})^B）、Theorem 5.1（この関係から非 Zariski 稠密性）。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.method_outline: 1) Section 2: F=f×f^{-1} を A2×A2 上で考え、周期曲線が存在しないこと（Bedford–Smillie）から問題を ⋃_n F^n(Δ_C) の非 Zariski 稠密性に帰着（Lemma 2.4）。2) Section 3: 数体上で f の周期点列の small height と Yuan/Thuillier の算術 equidistribution、Yuan–Zhang の arithmetic Hodge index theorem を用い、各 place で G+_{f,v}=αG−_{f,v} を導く（Prop 3.8）。Cantat–Dujardin の rigidity（Theorem 3.2）で剰余項の消去に使う。3) Section 4: Böttcher 座標 φ± により、この比例関係を (φ+∘f^N0)^A=(φ−∘f^{-N0})^B という解析的関係に翻訳（Prop 4.1）。4) Section 4.3: 数体上から C 上へ specialization（spreading out）で拡張（Prop 4.2）。5) Section 5: 函数体 C(Ĉ) 上で Xie の algebraization criterion（Theorem 5.2）を適用し、Böttcher 関係から非 Zariski 稠密性を導く（Theorem 5.1）。6) Theorem A と Theorem 5.5 を組み合わせて結論。既存の道具は BS91, Yuan/Thuillier, YZ17, CD26, Xie24、新しい部分は Green 関数の比例から Böttcher 関係を経て非稠密性へ至る算術幾何的連鎖の構成と、Hénon 型への適用。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.research_connection: 論文に明記された接点: (i) arithmetic dynamics — canonical height h_f、periodic points、Bogomolov 型（Theorem 5.5）、Yuan–Zhang の Arakelov 幾何。(ii) complex dynamics — Hénon 写像の Green 関数・Böttcher 座標・平衡測度（Bedford–Smillie, Hubbard–Oberste-Vorth）、Cantat–Dujardin の rigidity。(iii) symbolic dynamics/1次元力学との直接の記述は確認できず。推測: Hénon 写像は複素力学系の文脈で Julia 集合的対象として関連するが、本論文は算術的・代数幾何的手法が主で、kneading や shift 空間の議論は使っていない。combinatorics on words や aperiodic order への直接の接続は本文中に明記なし。computer-assisted proofs は使っておらず、AI 未使用の明示的声明のみ。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.reading_guide: 前提知識: 算術力学（canonical height、adelic line bundle、equidistribution, arithmetic Hodge index）、複素 Hénon 写像の Green 関数と Böttcher 座標、代数幾何（Zariski 主定理、特異点解消、specialization）。最初に読むべきは Theorem A（p.2）、次に Section 2 の Lemma 2.3–2.4（幾何的還元）、Prop 3.8 とその証明の流れ、Prop 4.1–4.2、Theorem 5.1 と Xie の Theorem 5.2。全文精読は算術幾何の準備（Section 3.2）が重いので、まず intro と Section 2・5 の骨格を追い、必要に応じて Section 3–4 の equidistribution 部分を精読するのが効率的。
follow_up_questions: Proposition 3.8 の比例定数 α は deg(D+_{N0})/deg(D−_{N0}) と明示されるが、Theorem A の involution σ の存在と α の値の間には具体的な関係があるか。
Xie の algebraization criterion（Theorem 5.2）の適用で、dim H = 2 を導く際に Lemma 2.2 が本質的だが、非 Zariski 稠密性の帰結を Hénon 型以外（一般の polynomial automorphism）に拡張できる障害は何か。
Theorem 5.5 の Bogomolov 型は数体上だが、函数体や p 進体上での類似（non-archimedean 版）は本論文の手法でどこまで可能か。

papers.title: Higher Realizability Toposes
papers.summary: Building on $\infty$-tripos theory, we develop a theory of realizability $\infty$-toposes. We apply $\infty$-tripos theory to construct the function, modified, and Krivine realizability $\infty$-toposes. We recover the Lawvere-Tierney nucleus $j$ that specifies local truth in each construction by exhibiting, for any $n\geq1$, a single family of Eilenberg-MacLane $n$-types whose fibre at an ambient truth value $p$ is contractible after sheafification precisely when $j(p)$ holds. In function realizability, we relate identity types to descriptive set theory. For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a univalent classifier $U_n$ of exact truncation height $n+1$. As maps from Baire space into $U_n$ vary, the sets of inputs admitting a global path from the assigned code to the terminal code are exactly the $G_δ$ subsets of Baire space. After exponentiation by Baire space, the analogous test against the constant map at the terminal code yields exactly the coanalytic sets, at the same truncation height. In modified realizability, a closed proof of local existence under a stable numerical precondition yields a total recursive function together with a coherent proof that its output satisfies the specification whenever the precondition holds. In Krivine realizability, contextual choice for $(n-1)$-truncated families over suitable $n$-types recovers the subterminal defining the Boolean localization. Binary cohomology distinguishes slices of Anel-Awodey-Barton's effective $\infty$-topos even when they share the same ordinary Hyland effective topos and their bases have equivalent spaces of global points. Hyland's effective topos thus occurs as the category of zero-types in infinitely many pairwise inequivalent realizability $\infty$-toposes (recovering Hyland's effective topos as the category of zero-types does not uniquely determine an effective $\infty$-topos).

papers.title: Higher Duality Theory: Geometric HoTT and Classifying $\infty$-Toposes
papers.summary: We develop geometric homotopy type theory (geometric HoTT), which gives a dependent language for constructions preserved by inverse images of geometric morphisms. We give a homotopy-coherent calculus for geometric HoTT and extend the classical duality between geometric logic and classifying toposes to Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes. For each geometric type theory, the $\infty$-category of contexts generated by its rules is equivalent to its classifying $\infty$-topos. As the theory varies, the classifier gives a duality of $(\infty,2)$-categories between geometric HoTT theories with interpretations and Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes with geometric morphisms. We then construct a universal family of classifying $\infty$-toposes whose fiber at each presentation of a theory is the classifying $\infty$-topos of that theory. We also construct a universal family of classifying $\infty$-toposes with coherent transport along Morita equivalences of theories. Geometric HoTT thus serves as an internal language for Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes, extending the role of geometric logic in classical topos theory to the realm of $\infty$-topos theory.

papers.title: General bounds for metric dimension of diameter-two graphs with applications
papers.summary: We study the metric dimension of several classes of graphs with diameter two. First, we establish a general lower bound for the metric dimension of graphs with diameter two in terms of their order and maximum degree. We then apply our results to Grassmann graphs, Moore graphs, and bilinear forms graphs. For Kneser graphs, we obtain new upper bounds, while for $G_q(n,2)$ Grassmann graphs we establish new upper bounds provided by constructions of resolving sets. For Moore graphs of diameter two, we derive improved lower bounds, and for $H_q(n,2)$ bilinear forms graphs, we obtain new upper and lower bounds on their metric dimension.

papers.title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
papers.summary: Let $G = *_λG_λ$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.

papers.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
papers.summary:
In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere.
  Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.

papers.title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
papers.summary:
A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends.
  We prove a stronger statement for at most countably many ends. Number the vertices of a ray, and let the type of a path that ends on the ray be the parity of the sum of its length and the number of its last vertex. A fan is mixed if it has infinitely many paths of each type, and a digraph is parity-safe if it has no odd cycle and no ray containing infinitely many vertices with a mixed fan to it. Yablo's graph (omega,<) is not parity-safe. Its variant with edges only between vertices of different parity has a kernel - it is parity-safe but not safe. Our main result is that a parity-safe digraph with at most countably many ends is kernel-perfect, and the claim for safe digraphs follows since safety implies parity-safety. The digraph may have any cardinality, and nothing is assumed about the structure of the ends, but the case of uncountably many ends remains open.

papers.title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
papers.summary: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem. We develop Gröbner bases for ideals of the free algebra and prove that the elements $e_k\oplusτ$, with $τ$ ranging over any set of permutations, form a Gröbner basis for the lexicographic ordering and for its opposite. This gives an algebraic form of the theorem of Backelin, West and Xin: the permutations avoiding all $k\cdots21\oplusτ$ and those avoiding all $12\cdots k\oplusτ$ are two monomial bases of one and the same quotient.

papers.title: The probability that two random generalized derangements have the same number of cycles
papers.summary: Using singularity analysis, we show that the probability that two independently and uniformly selected generalized derangements of size $n$ have the same number of cycles is asymptotically the same as the corresponding probability for unrestricted permutations, namely, $\sim \frac{1}{2\sqrt{π\log n}}\;.$

papers.title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(α,β)$-system (1.7). We obtain large-range spectral instability and small-range stability results valid for arbitrary eccentricity. The restricted $(n+1)$-body problem arises as a special case of this system. Accordingly, we derive several criteria for spectral instability and linear stability for this problem. As a final application, we establish some stability results of elliptic relative equilibria for massless particle under some special central configurations.

papers.title: TPTL-dist: A Formalised Calculus with Proof Automation for Verifying Real-Time Distributed Systems
papers.summary: We introduce TPTL-dist, a temporal logic and labelled sequent calculus for specifying and verifying real-time distributed systems. TPTL-dist is formalised in Agda to provide machine-checked correctness and tool support, including automation through a proof search that runs inside Agda. The logic extends Timed Propositional Temporal Logic (TPTL) with past operators, freeze quantification, comparisons between time expressions, domain-specific atoms, and an induction principle on time. We provide a world-based semantics, develop an interval-annotated calculus, and establish its soundness w.r.t. the semantics. To demonstrate its expressiveness, we encode standard distributed system patterns, and we carry out a mechanised proof of a key real-time property of the Pistis Byzantine broadcast protocol. Our results show that TPTL-dist provides a uniform, mechanised framework for reasoning about temporal properties of distributed systems.

papers.title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC
papers.summary: Binary classification from positive-only samples is a variant of PAC learning in which the learner receives i.i.d. samples only from the positive region of an unknown target concept, but is evaluated on the full distribution. Improper learnability in this model has a textbook characterization, whereas proper learnability has remained open for decades. Recent work characterized it for learners with access to randomness, and showed that, unlike in PAC learning, some classes are properly learnable with randomness but not without it, leaving the deterministic case open. We show that this case cannot be resolved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC): there is a class of VC dimension two whose deterministic proper learnability is independent of ZFC, even though a randomized learner provably learns it. Moreover, no dimension of finite character, a desirable property shared by most dimensions in learning theory, characterizes deterministic proper learnability. We also show that the size of the domain is decisive. In ZFC, deterministic proper learnability has a combinatorial characterization on every domain whose cardinality is below a certain threshold, including every countable domain. In contrast, this characterization fails on every domain of sufficiently large cardinality. Under the generalized continuum hypothesis, this threshold is sharp: it is the exact cardinality at which the characterization starts to fail. Finally, our proofs introduce new tools, based on the Erdos--Rado partition theorem, that may be of broader interest.

papers.title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$ and the number $\ell_i(G)$ of cycles of each possible length $i \geq 1$ in $G$. We define \[ \ell(G) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{\ell_i(G)}{(d - 1)^i}\] and we prove with $λ= (d - 1)\log(1 + 1/(d - 1))$ that for all $d \geq 2$, \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \exp(λ\ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n),\] where $S_d(n)$ denotes $2^{-dn/2}\binom{d}{d/2}^n$. The bound sharply improves the lower bound of Lieb, Wu and Schrijver, and gives good estimates for $\varepsilon(G)$ for various graphs, such as integer lattices. The bound is almost tight for random regular graphs, and we conjecture for each even $d \geq 4$ that there exists a constant $c_d > 0$ such that $\varepsilon(G) \leq \exp(c_dλ\ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n)$ for every $n$-vertex $d$-regular pseudograph.

papers.title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
papers.summary: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.

papers.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
papers.summary: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

papers.title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
papers.summary: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(Ω(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(Ω(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(Ω(n^{6/7-ε})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms. Our proof technique is based on deriving properties of bisectors under various norms.

papers.title: An $n^{1/O(\log^* n)}$ Lower Bound for Online Coloring of $k$-Colorable Graphs
papers.summary: In online coloring, the vertices of a graph arrive one at a time with their edges to earlier vertices, and each vertex must be colored irrevocably on arrival. For graphs promised to be $k$-colorable, with $k\ge 3$ fixed, the best deterministic algorithms use $n^{1-Θ(1/k^2)}$ colors, while the best lower bound was Vishwanathan's $Ω(\log^{k-1}n)$ from 1990 until Li recently proved $2^{Ω((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})}$. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we prove a lower bound of $n^{1/(\log^*n+3)}$ colors for deterministic online algorithms on $n$-vertex $k$-colorable graphs, and the same lower bound in expectation for randomized online algorithms. Both bounds hold on a single triangle-free $3$-colorable graph: even an algorithm that is shown this graph in advance, but is not told which of its vertices each arriving vertex is, can be forced to use this many colors by a suitable arrival order. The hard instances are iterated blow-ups of a clique, in which every vertex becomes a block of independent vertices and every edge a private server in the earlier block; each blow-up keeps the forced colors and replaces the chromatic number $χ$ by about $\logχ$, so about $\log^*n$ blow-ups bring it down to $k$. We also show that deterministic lower bounds for different values of $k\ge 3$ are polynomially equivalent, and that no adversary presenting such iterated blow-ups can force more than $n^{1/(\log^*n-O(1))}$ colors. All numbered results are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
papers.summary: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is described through a limiting distribution of correlated Euler products, for which we give an atomlessness argument. The classification resolves the distinct-index formulation of the universal-implication conjecture.

papers.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
papers.summary: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.

papers.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
papers.summary: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

papers.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
papers.summary: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.

papers.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-β\)-transformations
papers.summary: We study the subshifts \(Ω_{-β,α}\) associated with the intermediate \(-β\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-βx+α\pmod1\), where \((β,α)\inΔ_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $Ω_{-β,α}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{β,α}=α/β\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((β,α)\) for which \(Ω_{-β,α}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(Δ_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.

papers.title: Rotational Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
papers.summary: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

papers.title: Hashing Theorems Modulo Rewrites and Binder Permutation Enables Equivalence Search over 200k Mathlib Theorems
papers.summary: Like all code, Lean libraries accumulate technical debt and structural deficiencies over the course of their development. A particular concern is duplicate theorems: different parts of a big library can unwittingly contain and prove the same theorem, duplicating maintenance efforts. Tools can help detect redundancy and clean up. For instance, Mathlib's duplicate-declarations linter compares theorem types syntactically after sorting top-level binders and erasing binder information and universe levels. If detecting an equivalence requires unfolding, reorientation, or logical transformations, it escapes this comparison. In this work, we present a method to detect theorems which are equivalent with regard to argument order and currying/uncurrying of dependent types. We implement our method for Lean. By applying it to Mathlib, a library of more than 200k theorems, we demonstrate that it is computationally cheap and scalable. We discuss how our work may enhance efforts to tackle the maintenance burden of Lean libraries.

papers.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
papers.summary: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.

papers.title: Concave Run Budgets and Restart Width
papers.summary:
A source-to-target path in an edge-labelled DAG uses each label in some number of maximal runs, with a label used in \(r\) runs charged according to a nondecreasing concave rational tariff \(f(r)\). We seek a path of total charge at most \(B\), or a shortest such path. We parameterize by restart width \(\wr\), the maximum number of labels that have already appeared and can still begin a new run at some vertex. It is at most live width but can be arbitrarily smaller.
  Let \(J_f(T)\) denote the number of distinct marginal rates of \(f\) up to horizon \(T\). A lazy-commitment dynamic program solves minimum charge and feasibility in \(J_f(T)^{\wr}\poly(N)\) time, allowing arbitrary per-label tariffs and unbounded charge magnitudes. Thus the problem is FPT whenever \(J_f\) is effectively subpolynomial. Conversely, for every fixed tariff with \(J_f(T)\ge T^δ\) eventually, feasibility is NP-complete and W[1]-hard in \(\wr\), even on planar bipartite DAGs of maximum degree three and treewidth two whose paths have equal length, and admits no \(g(\wr)N^{o(\wr)}\) algorithm under ETH. The reduction uses positive pairwise Jensen-gap charges, requires no denominator assumption, and covers harmonic, geometric, and power-law tariffs. A \(k\)-colour clique instance has width at most \(2k+1\), improved to \(k+1\) for polynomially bounded denominators.
  We further exhibit arbitrarily close tariffs with opposite parameterized complexity, give an FPT budget-relaxing scheme and accuracy obstruction, establish few-label hardness and W[P]-membership, and identify separate hardness from binary-encoded lengths. Oscillating plan growth and non-effective subpolynomial bounds remain open.

papers.title: Products of supersoluble groups
papers.summary: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.

papers.title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
papers.summary: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.

papers.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
papers.summary: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincaré-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.

papers.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
papers.summary:
Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,ω$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$).
  Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrarily high orders are dense in the space of parametric families intersecting $\mathcal N(L)$. If $r\le\infty$ and $L$ is sectionally dissipative, this implies density of families possessing infinitely many coexisting stable periodic orbits for some open set of parameter values.

papers.title: A detailed verification of Neary's PCP(5) construction
papers.summary: Neary proved that the Post correspondence problem remains undecidable for instances with five pairs of words. We give a detailed verification of his construction. We first verify the undecidability of the restricted binary tag-system halting problem used in the reduction. We then prove both directions of the reduction to the five-pair problem, using the longer closing pair proposed by Rote. In particular, we show that every solution of the constructed PCP instance yields a halting computation of the simulated tag system.

papers.title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
papers.summary: H. Duan, H. Liu, Y. Long and W. Wang \cite{DLLW24} conjectured that if a compact star-shaped hypersurface in ${\bf R}^{2n}$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics, then each of them has nonzero mean index. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $Σ$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $Σ$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them are irrationally elliptic.

papers.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
papers.summary: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least $m$ distinct hyperbolic limit cycles. We thank GPT-6 Astra for helping us compare earlier constructions, identify the main obstacle to extending them, and develop the present approach.

papers.title: The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity
papers.summary: In their 2007 paper on the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences, Liu and Wang conjectured that the Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity. We completely solve their conjecture by showing that this transformation preserves strong $q$-log-convexity. More generally, we provide a sufficient condition for a linear transformation, defined by a triangular array satisfying a certain three-term recurrence relation, to preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. As applications, we show that both the $r$-colored Eulerian transformation and the $m$-Stirling Eulerian transformation preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. In particular, we confirm a conjecture due to Liu and Zhu, which states that the Eulerian transformation of type $B$ preserves log-convexity.

papers.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
papers.summary: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
papers.summary: A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 23 (1977), 127--138] proved that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge6$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(3|V(G)|-6)/2$, and this bound is sharp for every even order at least 6. Fabres, Kothari and Carvalho [J. Graph Theory 96 (2021), 490--509] proved that every minimal 2-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge12$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(5|V(G)|-20)/2$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (2026), 559--606] characterized minimal matching covered bipartite graphs $G$ with $|E(G)|=(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ in terms of special trees. They also conjectured that, for every integer $k\ge1$, there exists an integer $N_k\le4k^2+2k$ such that every minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge N_k$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(2k+1)(|V(G)|-2k)/2$. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for $k\ge3$ and prove that the upper bound is sharp for every even order at least $6k$ ($k\ge3$).

papers.title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
papers.summary: Thomassé conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.

papers.title: Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$
papers.summary: We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $α$ can be chosen with $[P,α,α]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $α$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,α,α,α]=1$, and with $[P,α,α]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.

papers.title: On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $σ$-permutable subgroups
papers.summary: Let $σ=\{σ_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $σ$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $σ_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $σ$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.

papers.title: On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4
papers.summary: A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable. Our proof combines Rofa's algebraic graceful labeling at the root with complementary labelings, an end-to-end leg-reversal construction placing $0$ at a leaf, and a two-leg reflection permutation placing $0$ at distance $2$ from the root.

papers.title: Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps
papers.summary: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Lattès families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.

papers.title: Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
papers.summary: We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that retains the full unitary class and is a convex combination of at most four classical grids. This measurement map embeds the five-square model into a seven-dimensional polytope whose vertices are the twelve classical Sudoku.

papers.title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
papers.summary: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the larger sum from degree four on.

papers.title: Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
papers.summary: We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced. This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique. Moreover, we prove the existence of invariant measures by the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov approach, and further establish the regularity of invariant measures by virtue of a control argument.

papers.title: Extremal adjacency and distance spectral radii of graph powers
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, \[ ρ(G^k)\geq ρ(P_n^k) \qquad\text{and}\qquad ρ_D(G^k)\leq ρ_D(P_n^k), \] where $P_n$ is the path of order $n$, and $ρ$ and $ρ_D$ are the adjacency and distance spectral radii, respectively. If $n\geq k+2$, equality in either inequality holds precisely when $G\cong P_n$. If $n\leq k+1$, every connected graph of order $n$ has complete $k$-th power, and both inequalities are equalities. The adjacency bound is proved by transferring a terminal vertex between pendant paths and applying a reflection rearrangement to a Rayleigh quotient. For the distance bound, a transfer of an entire pendant path is required; a Schur-complement comparison and estimates for the antisymmetric subspace of a path-power distance matrix yield the result. We also give examples showing why the two adjacency arguments do not extend directly to the distance spectral radius.

papers.title: A transitive $C^{1+α}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
papers.summary: Let $0<α\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

papers.title: Probabilistic Timed Automata with Multiple Sure and Threshold Objectives
papers.summary: Probabilistic timed automata extend the classical timed automata formalism with discrete probabilistic choice over edges. We consider the case of the verification of a combination of multiple objectives of probabilistic timed automata, where the objectives can be non-probabilistic (referring to sure satisfaction of all behaviors) and probabilistic (referring to a probability threshold), and refer to reachability or $ω$-regular properties on executions expressed using parity conditions. We show that existing algorithms for multiple objectives for finite-state Markov decision processes can be applied, using the classical region-graph construction, to obtain algorithms for the corresponding objectives of probabilistic timed automata. In particular, the verification of a probabilistic timed automata against multiple probabilistic-threshold sink-reachability objectives subject to the almost-sure divergence of time is EXPTIME-complete, while verification against the combination of a sure property, including sure divergence of time, and a single probabilistic-threshold parity objective is in NEXPTIME $\cap$ coNEXPTIME.

papers.title: Two Primes Suffice for Definable Graph Canonisation
papers.summary: We study inflationary fixed-point logic on finite simple graphs with unordered vertices and an ordered number sort. For a prime $r$, the quantifier $M_r$ tests whether the number of relations satisfying a formula is nonzero modulo $r$. For any distinct primes $p$ and $q$, the logic with $M_p$ and $M_q$ defines the adjacency matrix of a canonical copy on the number sort. On labelled inputs this matrix is computable in deterministic polynomial time with an oracle that tests whether the number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean circuit is nonzero modulo $p$. For each prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ alone cannot define a canonical copy on all graphs. The primes also differ on Boolean queries. There is a single first-order formula $β(S)$ on vertex sets such that $M_q S β(S)$ is undefinable with $M_p$ alone whenever $p \ne q$. For a positive integer-valued function $g$, consider the class of all graphs $G$ with at most $g(|V(G)|)$ automorphisms. For each fixed prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ canonises this class exactly when $g$ is bounded.

papers.title: A new upper bound for the Erdős--Szekeres conjecture
papers.summary: Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}. \] In this article, we further improve the upper bound by showing that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{1/3})}. \]

papers.title: Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results
papers.summary:
A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $χ_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $χ_o(G)$ are known. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on $χ_o(G)$ for several graph classes.
  In particular, we obtain the following results:
  1. For every block-cactus graph $G$, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq \max \{5,ω(G)+1\}$, where $ω(G)$ denotes the clique number of $G$.
  2. For block graphs and proper interval graphs, we establish the bounds $ω(G) \leq χ_o(G) \leq ω(G)+1$.
  3. For a bipartite circle graph, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq 6$. This settles an open question asked by Davis et al., 2026.
  4. For every biconvex bipartite graph $G$, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq 5$.
  5. For $C_4$-free cographs $G$, we establish the bound $χ_o(G) \leq ω(G)+1$.
  Moreover, we characterize block graphs, proper interval graphs, and cactus graphs based on their odd chromatic number.

papers.title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
papers.summary: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.

papers.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series
papers.summary: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

papers.title: $\mathsf{Y} \& \mathsf{X}$: Intermediate Logics of Convex Hulls and Cross-Polytopes
papers.summary: We investigate two logics of geometric Kripke frames: $\mathsf{Y}$, defined by finite convex hulls, and $\mathsf{X}$, defined by cross-polytopes. We characterize the validity of the Kreisel--Putnam axiom on convex hull frames by means of convex independence. Our main technical results concern several reductions obtained using two translations, $C$ and $D$. In particular, we show that $\mathsf{X}$ is invariant under $C$, while $\mathsf{Y}$ is invariant under $D$. Moreover, the same translation $D$ reduces Medvedev logic to every logic in the interval $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$, where $\mathsf{Y}'$ is a naturally defined intermediate logic strictly between $\mathsf{Y}$ and $\mathsf{Med}$. Together with geometric arguments, these reductions establish that $\mathsf{Y}$, $\mathsf{X}$, and $\mathsf{Cheq}$ are pairwise incomparable, while each lies strictly between $\mathsf{PL}$ and Medvedev logic. We also prove that every logic in $[\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{Med}]$ is not finitely axiomatizable and that this interval contains continuum many distinct logics. In addition, every logic in $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$ is undecidable. We prove that $\mathsf{X}$ is undecidable and $\mathsf{Y}\in Π^0_1$. In particular, we show that it is decidable whether a finite poset is isomorphic to a finite convex hull frame, and that the logics determined by configurations of a bounded number of points are decidable. Finally, we extend our study to infinite convex hull frames. We show that inclusion yields $\mathsf{KC}$, whereas reverse inclusion yields $\mathsf{IPC}$. For the latter result, we use the Cantor set to construct $p$-morphisms onto arbitrary finite rooted frames.

papers.title: Quaternary games with infinite misère quotients
papers.summary: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its misère quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their misère quotients are infinite. For \texttt{0.3312}, as well as many other wild quaternary games, we carry out computations and observations.
