In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

papers.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
papers.summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

papers.title: A logarithmic saving in the sum-free subset problem
papers.summary: For every sufficiently large $n$ there is a set of $n$ positive integers, all at most $n^2$, whose largest sum-free subset has size at most $n/3+O(n/\log n)$. We bound the number of small divisible elements in a dense set with few Schur triples. A fixed-accuracy cyclic model gives a rotation, and the original integer triple count controls its density at the required scale.

papers.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
papers.summary: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical) and 10 desirable properties, which we argue are the conditions for safely optimising a measure. In a Curry-Howard kernel, 5 machine-checked proofs that the primes are infinite show that raw syntax cannot tell a rewrite from a new argument, that dependency-based and structural measures reproduce the intuitive ordering (Euclid rewritten < Goldbach < Furstenberg), and that semantic measures invert it: Furstenberg's topological proof produces exactly Euclid's witness. A replication in Lean 4/Mathlib (3 theorems, 19 proofs, 18 measures) confirms that dependency-closure measures track intuition best, and shows that equality of normal forms never holds between differently written versions of the same argument, that proofs by citation look unlike the arguments they cite, and that proof irrelevance cannot distinguish any two proofs. We argue for reporting dissimilarity as a multi-level profile, extend the measures to proofs of different theorems, and discuss uses, from detecting duplicated AI proofs and orchestrating prover agents to interpreting AI proofs via their nearest human-understandable counterparts. Code, Lean sources and data are released.

papers.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
papers.summary: Let $Γ$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(Γ)$ is edge-transitive, then $Γ$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(Γ)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

papers.title: On equational $\mathfrak{X}$-domains
papers.summary: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups containing all abelian groups. We introduce and investigate equational $\X$-domains as a generalization of equational domains in algebraic geometry over groups. We characterize these groups by means of systems of equations associated with the identities of $\X$, and describe the radical and coordinate group of the union of two coordinate axes. We also extend classical characterizations of coordinate groups of irreducible algebraic sets, involving discrimination and universal theories, to the setting of equational $\X$-domains. Finally, we establish two construction results: under suitable malnormality, amalgamated free products are equational $\X$-domains; moreover, a restricted regular wreath product of two nontrivial groups is an equational $\X$-domain if and only if its base group is an equational $\X$-domain.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33113v1.title: 最大次数フィルトレーション、Koszul複体、および多色置換Wordle
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33113v1.summary: 本論文は、完全に一次因子に分解する多変数多項式によって生成されるイデアル族のKoszul分解を研究する。動機となる例はKutinとSmithlineによるゲーム「Permutation Wordle」および「Multicolor Permutation Wordle」に関する研究に由来し、そこでの未解決問題（予想4.5）を解決する。選択した生成元に対し、Koszul微分が最大次数フィルトレーションに関してstrictであり、より一般に座標が連続整数からなる任意の多次数においてstrictであることを示す。この結果得られる次元の数え上げによってKutin–Smithlineの予想が解決される。証明は帰納法であり、各帰納ステップは反復である。中核となる議論は人間によって生成されたもので、本証明はAIの支援を受けて開発され、多次数還元の反復とmapping cone帰納法を分離する。この方法により、複体の最高次数までのリフトの整合性を追跡する必要が回避される。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33113v1.appendix: 関連分野: combinatorics on words（語の組合せ論、文字列・置換に由来するゲームの解析）、computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics（AI支援による証明開発）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32875v1.title: 射影多様体の有理自己写像の周期点の数え上げ
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32875v1.summary: 滑らかな射影多様体の優越的有理自己写像について、孤立周期点の数の漸近挙動を研究する。まず、写像の反復の次数を用いてこの数の上界を与え、Dinh--Nguyen--Truong の定理を任意標数に拡張する。この手法は純粋に代数的であり、正閉電流の密度理論を経由しない。次に、標数 0 の体上の曲面の双有理自己写像について、孤立周期点の正確な漸近増加を確立する。そのために、Moriwaki の高さの理論を用いて Jonsson--Reschke の議論を ℚ 上の任意の有限生成体に拡張する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32875v1.appendix: 関連分野: arithmetic dynamics（高さ理論、周期点の数え上げ）、complex and one-dimensional real dynamics（周期点の漸近挙動に関連）。
